This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court passed the following:
 JUDGMENT

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act (hereinafter referred to as "Act")
has been preferred by the appellants/claimants against the award dated 01.11.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Seoni in Claim Case No. 117/2019 whereby claim petition has been dismissed on the ground that accident by offending vehicle itself has not been found proved.
2. The brief facts of the case are that on 03.12.2018 deceased Bhagwati Bai was going to Madhava with his brother Sunil Yadav (AW-2) on his motorcycle as pillion rider.
At about 5:00 pm when they reached near the field of Omprakash Pandey, respondent No.1 driving the tractor bearing registration No. MP-22-AB-0584 rashly and negligently dashed the Bhagwati Bai.
She suffered grievous injuries.
She was brought to the District Hospital Seoni for treatment, where Doctor declared her dead.
Deceased at the time of accident was of 45 years of age, she was getting pension of Rs. 7,888/- per month and by working as labourer was also earning Rs. 6000/- per month.
Appellants/claimants were dependent on the deceased.
Therefore, they filed the claim petition for the compensation of Rs. 34,50,000/-.
3. Respondents No. 1 and 2 controverted fact of accident with for the allegation that they have falsely been implicated in this case.
Respondent No. 3/insurance company in its reply stated that tractor No. MP-22-AB-0584 allegedly involved in the accident was not insured with insurance company.
The fact of the accident has also not been proved.
The claim petition has been preferred in collusion with the owner of the tractor and police and on these ground, insurance company prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

4. Learned claim tribunal in the impugned award found that no accident took place by the tractor No. MP-22-AB-0584 and in alternative returned a finding that motorcyclist Sunil Yadav has driven his motorcycle No. MH-35-U-3024 rashly and negligently which caused accident.

On this ground,
claim tribunal dismissed the claim petition.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that learned claims tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim petition.
Accident by the offending tractor was proved by the evidence on record.
Learned claim tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence in right perspective.

Learned counsel for the appellants to bolster his submission has also drawn attention of this Court towards the para 10 of the impugned award and para 2 of the statement of Vishnu (PW-1).
6.

Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company has supported the award passed by the claim tribunal and submitted that appellants/claimants have failed to prove that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending tractor.
Actually accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by the brother of the deceased on which she was pillion rider.
Tractor was falsely implicated.

Learned claims tribunal has appreciated the evidence in right perspective and dismissed the claim petition, which does not bear any factual and legality,
appeal being devoid of merit and deserves to be dismissed.

2
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award along with record.
8. Learned claims tribunal in the impugned award has elaborately discussed the evidence on record.
In paragraph 17 of the impugned award it has been mentioned that Vishnu Yadav (AW-1) has admitted in cross-examination's para 10 of his deposition that he did not witness the accident.
He has narrated this at the instance of his maternal uncle Sunil Yadav (AW/2).
Sunil Yadav (AW-2) has narrated about the incident in his court statement.
He has admitted that in Ex. P/8, it is mentioned that accident took place due to fall of the motorcycle.
He has also admitted this fact in first information report (Ex. P/2).
He has further admitted that he has not made complaint before the senior officer against the grounds of accident mentioned in Ex. P/2 and Ex. P/8.

In Ex. P/2 and Ex.
P/8 are the document, which have been relied upon by the claimants.
Ex. P/8 has been written at the instance of Sunil Yadav (AW-2).

Though his signature on this document has not been obtained,
even then the scribe of this document has mentioned that it has been written on the information given by the Sunil Kumar (AW/2) (brother of the deceased).

Learned claims tribunal has taken into account the narration of these documents and concluded that actually accident took place by the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by Sunil Yadav (AW/2) brother of the deceased and on this basis and taking other evidence on record, discussing the judgment cited by both the side,
learned claims tribunal dismissed the claim petition.
9.
In considered opinion of this Court, nothing can be pointed out by the counsel for the appellants/claimants that finding is perverse, therefore, impugned award needs no interference from this court.
The appeal being devoid of any substance is hereby dismissed.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Digitally L.R.signed by LALIT SINGH RANA Date:
